question: A skin biopsy shows: Bacteriological Index 3+ on Ziehl-Neelsen staining, numerous lipid-laden macrophages (Virchow cells/foam cells) packed with acid-fast bacilli, and a clear band of uninvolved collagen (Grenz zone) separating the epidermis from the dermal infiltrate. What type of leprosy does this represent?

answers.text: Lepromatous leprosy with dominant Th2 (humoral) and weak Th1 (cell-mediated) response

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! High BI (3+), foam cells (Virchow cells) laden with bacilli, and the Grenz zone are pathognomonic for lepromatous leprosy (LL). Weak Th1 immunity means macrophages cannot kill *M. leprae* → unrestricted bacillary multiplication. The Grenz zone (clear subepidermal collagen band) is UNIQUE to lepromatous leprosy — no other granulomatous skin disease has this feature.

answers.text: Tuberculoid leprosy with strong Th1 (cell-mediated) immune response

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Tuberculoid leprosy has STRONG Th1 immunity with well-formed epithelioid granulomas, Langhans giant cells, and very few or absent bacilli (BI 0–1). Granulomas extend right up to the epidermis — there is NO Grenz zone. The strong cell-mediated response limits bacterial multiplication.

answers.text: Borderline tuberculoid leprosy with moderate granulomatous response

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Borderline tuberculoid (BT) shows moderate Th1 response with less well-organised granulomas than TT. BI is typically 1–2+. While it occupies the spectrum, the combination of BI 3+, foam cells, and a clear Grenz zone specifically defines the lepromatous pole.

answers.text: Indeterminate leprosy with early undifferentiated immune response

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Indeterminate leprosy is the earliest form with non-specific perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate. It has not differentiated toward either pole — no foam cells, no epithelioid granulomas, no Grenz zone. It may evolve toward any point on the Ridley-Jopling spectrum.

overallFeedback.feedback: Leprosy histopathology summary: TT = epithelioid granulomas reaching epidermis, few/no AFB, strong Th1; LL = foam cells (Virchow cells), Grenz zone, many AFB (BI 4–6+), weak Th1/dominant Th2. The immune response determines the histological picture and bacillary load.

The Grenz zone + foam cells + high BI = lepromatous leprosy. This triad is a pathology examination favourite. The Grenz zone is specific to LL — remember it means 'border zone' in German (a clear collagen band separating epidermis from the granulomatous infiltrate below).
